scope: Cambridge Part III General Relativity examinations 2001–2012

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1: define a linear connection; derive the unique symmetric metric connection and its coefficients; prove that the difference between two symmetric metric connections is a tensor; and characterize connections with the same geodesics by S^a_bc = 2 delta^a_(b V_c), including determination of V.
problems.short_topic: Levi-Civita and projectively equivalent connections
problems.disposition_rationale: A coherent, self-contained tensor-analysis parent that moves from the Levi-Civita formula to the tensorial difference of connections and the nontrivial same-geodesic condition; it fits Weinberg Chapter 4 without splitting any stage.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: essay on gauge-invariant linearized vacuum perturbations of Minkowski spacetime, with permission to use information from the lecture handout supplied with the examination.
problems.short_topic: Gauge-invariant linearized vacuum gravity
problems.disposition_rationale: The topic directly fits the weak-field and gravitational-wave material in Chapter 10, but adaptation must replace the broad essay instruction with an auditable complete task and must either locate the optional lecture handout or supply every convention and formula used from it.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3: vary the printed Brans-Dicke action with scalar Phi, coupling omega, and matter Lagrangian to derive the metric field equation and the scalar equation Box Phi = 8 pi G T/(3 + 2 omega), using all three supplied metric-variation identities.
problems.short_topic: Brans-Dicke action and field equations
problems.disposition_rationale: This is a strong complete parent for Weinberg's Brans-Dicke section: the action, target equations, and variation identities are printed together and must all be retained while converting the paper's signature and curvature conventions.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4: for the printed 1+1 dimensional de Sitter and anti-de Sitter metrics, state every coordinate range and compare geodesics, conformal structure, and horizons in an essay.
problems.short_topic: Two-dimensional de Sitter and anti-de Sitter geometry
problems.disposition_rationale: The paired metrics make a useful complete comparison of maximally symmetric Lorentzian spaces for Chapter 13; a faithful exercise must retain both spacetimes and all three requested comparison themes rather than extracting only the de Sitter part.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1: prove the Ricci identity for a vector from the front-page curvature convention; generalize the commutator to arbitrary-valence tensors; prove symmetry of second scalar derivatives; compute and simplify phi_;(lm)n and phi_;l[mn]; and prove T^ik_;ik = T^ik_;ki for an arbitrary rank-two contravariant tensor.
problems.short_topic: Ricci identities and commuted covariant derivatives
problems.disposition_rationale: A well-sequenced curvature exercise that progresses from vectors to general tensors and then tests scalar and rank-two contractions; the front-page sign convention is an essential dependency that must accompany the parent during conversion to Chapter 6 notation.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: essay covering the Pound-Rebka experiment and its implications, the strong principle of equivalence, and a derivation of Einstein's field equations for a perfect fluid.
problems.short_topic: Redshift, equivalence, and Einstein equations
problems.disposition_rationale: Although broad and essay-form, the requested chain from experimental redshift through equivalence to the perfect-fluid field equations is pedagogically coherent for Chapter 7; selection requires preserving all three components and supplying explicit solution criteria rather than reducing it to a generic equivalence-principle prompt.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3: use the printed velocity-potential action for a perfect fluid to derive four-velocity normalization, dp/dh = n, number conservation, the stress tensor, and evolution equations for n, rho, and u^a; then take the stated static weak-field and slow-motion limit, obtain the linearized fluid equations, and interpret them.
problems.short_topic: Variational perfect fluid and Newtonian limit
problems.disposition_rationale: The action, thermodynamic relations, conservation laws, stress tensor, and Newtonian check form one connected variational parent suitable for Chapter 12; the weak-field metric and all stated approximations are indispensable and cannot be detached as a separate exercise.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4: essay on horizons in general relativity, including definitions and examples.
problems.short_topic: General-relativistic horizons
problems.disposition_rationale: The one-line essay request supplies no spacetime, definitions, assumptions, or bounded derivation, so a purported complete solution would depend almost entirely on invented scope; the more structured de Sitter, Schwarzschild, and conformal-horizon parents in this inventory are better fits.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1: express and extend Lie derivatives from scalars and vectors to covectors and (1,1) tensors, explain the arbitrary-tensor extension, prove the Lie-derivative commutator identity, develop the linear and commutator closure properties of Killing fields, and prove that the stationary and axial Killing fields of an asymptotically flat rotating star commute, using the optional Jacobi-identity hint.
problems.short_topic: Lie derivatives and the Killing algebra of a rotating star
problems.disposition_rationale: This complete parent links the algebraic definition of Lie differentiation to the global symmetry algebra of a rotating spacetime and is a strong Chapter 13 exercise; the asymptotic coordinate conditions and Jacobi hint must remain with it.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: essay on gauge-invariant linearized vacuum perturbations of Minkowski spacetime, with permission to use the lecture handout supplied with the examination.
problems.short_topic: Gauge-invariant linearized vacuum gravity
problems.disposition_rationale: The wording and optional lecture-handout dependency repeat the 2001 Paper 68 Question 2 prompt essentially verbatim, so retaining both would not add a distinct parent problem.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3: from the printed source-free electromagnetic action prove the Bianchi identity, derive Maxwell's equation by varying A_a, obtain the stress tensor variationally, analyze when stress-tensor conservation implies Maxwell's equation, and prove equivalence to the printed first-order Palatini action by independent variation of antisymmetric F^ab and A_a; the principle of equivalence may be assumed.
problems.short_topic: Maxwell action, stress tensor, and Palatini form
problems.disposition_rationale: A complete action-principle parent with three mutually reinforcing derivations and a clearly stated nonsingularity proviso; it belongs in Chapter 12 and must retain both actions and the conservation-law qualification.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4: compactify Minkowski spacetime in spherical coordinates using u, v, p, q, T, and R; derive the printed Einstein-static-universe conformal metric; state the ranges of every listed coordinate; and discuss the asymptotic behavior of Minkowski geodesics in the unphysical spacetime.
problems.short_topic: Conformal compactification of Minkowski spacetime
problems.disposition_rationale: The fully specified transformation chain gives a rigorous global-structure exercise for the special-relativistic spacetime of Chapter 2; all coordinate ranges and the geodesic-endpoint discussion are integral, and no supplied figure is present.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1: define a symmetric linear connection and covariant derivative; prove the sum, product, and scalar properties of the commutator Delta_ab; define the Riemann tensor through its action on a vector; derive its action on a covector and a (1,2) tensor and its first antisymmetry; and derive both Bianchi identities from successive scalar derivatives.
problems.short_topic: Curvature from commuted covariant derivatives
problems.disposition_rationale: This is a particularly complete construction of curvature and both Bianchi identities from the derivative commutator, exactly matching Chapter 6; the uncommon index placement in the source must be converted carefully rather than copied mechanically.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: state and discuss the strong principle of equivalence, then give a heuristic derivation of G_ik + Lambda g_ik = -8 pi G T_ik using the supplied Newtonian Ricci component R^N_00 = -nabla^2 phi.
problems.short_topic: Equivalence principle and heuristic Einstein equation
problems.disposition_rationale: A compact, bounded version of the equivalence-to-field-equation argument for Chapter 7, with the exact Newtonian matching datum printed as a hint; the cosmological term and the paper's opposite sign convention must both be preserved and reconciled.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3: for the stated large, slowly rotating thin spherical shell, source density, four-velocity, and interior metric ansatz, derive -A = C = GM/R and B_alpha = (4 GM Omega/3R)(y,-x,0), then discuss interior timelike geodesics and the Lense-Thirring effect, retaining the lecture-handout permission and supplied l=1 Laplacian hint.
problems.short_topic: Frame dragging inside a rotating shell
problems.disposition_rationale: A strong post-Newtonian frame-dragging parent for Chapter 9 with a complete source model, scaling assumptions, target fields, and spherical-harmonic hint; the optional lecture handout is not cached with the paper, so any selected version must insert rather than silently assume formulas taken from it.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4: for the printed 1+1 dimensional de Sitter and anti-de Sitter metrics, state every coordinate range and compare geodesics, conformal structure, and horizons in an essay.
problems.short_topic: Two-dimensional de Sitter and anti-de Sitter geometry
problems.disposition_rationale: Apart from immaterial punctuation, this repeats the full 2001 Paper 68 Question 4 comparison of the same two metrics, coordinate ranges, geodesics, conformal structure, and horizons.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1: derive component formulas for Lie derivatives of a scalar and vector, prove their covariant form, derive Killing's equation and the second-derivative curvature identity, obtain the coupled transport equations for a Killing field and its first derivative along an arbitrary curve, prove vanishing from zero initial data, and determine the maximal number of independent Killing fields in dimension n.
problems.short_topic: Killing-field transport and maximal symmetry bound
problems.disposition_rationale: The transport system gives a particularly effective proof of the dimension bound on an isometry algebra and is a strong Chapter 13 parent; every preliminary Lie-derivative and curvature step is needed for the final global uniqueness argument.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: essay on the role of curvature in general relativity and a carefully qualified derivation of Einstein's equations, emphasizing freely falling frames, relative acceleration of neighboring freely falling particles, and nonzero Riemann curvature.
problems.short_topic: Curvature, geodesic deviation, and field equations
problems.disposition_rationale: Despite its essay form, the prompt names a precise conceptual chain from local inertial frames through tensorial geodesic deviation to curvature and field dynamics, making it usable as a Chapter 6 synthesis if all requested assumptions and links are explicitly assessed.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3: derive the printed linearized Schwarzschild metric from the point-mass stress tensor; derive the equatorial null-geodesic equation in u = r_S/r; identify E and h; and determine the existence and stability of special circular null orbits, retaining the permission to use the supplied lecture handout.
problems.short_topic: Linearized Schwarzschild null orbits
problems.disposition_rationale: This connects weak-field sourcing to an observable geodesic problem and fits Chapter 8, but the circular-orbit conclusion pushes the linearized approximation to its limit and must be discussed critically; any formula borrowed from the uncached optional handout must be inserted.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4: compactify Minkowski spacetime using u, v, p, q, T, and R; derive the printed conformal metric; state all coordinate ranges; discuss asymptotic geodesics; and determine its horizon structure.
problems.short_topic: Minkowski conformal boundary and horizons
problems.disposition_rationale: It repeats the entire 2003 Paper 54 Question 4 construction and geodesic analysis nearly verbatim, adding only a final explicit request about horizons; that small extension does not justify a second complete parent.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1: establish all four printed algebraic Riemann symmetries, the differential and contracted Bianchi identities, the Ricci identity for vectors and its covector version, and the final twice-contracted derivative identity for the Riemann tensor.
problems.short_topic: Riemann symmetries and Bianchi identities
problems.disposition_rationale: A dense but self-contained Chapter 6 consolidation that explicitly includes algebraic symmetries, both levels of Bianchi contraction, and vector/covector commutators; the front-page curvature convention is required for every sign.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: analyze the printed covariant scalar theory of Newtonian gravity, with its particle momentum law, mass definition, Minkowski metric, and sourced scalar equation, and answer parts (a)-(c) on the Eotvos experiment, Pound-Rebka redshift, and solar light bending with reasons.
problems.short_topic: Experimental tests of a covariant scalar gravity theory
problems.disposition_rationale: The explicit alternative dynamics lets Chapter 3 test exactly what the equivalence principle and classic observations require, and all three experimental subparts are needed to expose the theory's successes and failure.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3: derive the linearized Riemann tensor and prove its gauge invariance; introduce and specify trace reversal and gauge to derive the sourced linearized Einstein wave equation; determine the metric perturbation produced by the stated null photon beam; and show that parallel photons are undeflected.
problems.short_topic: Gauge-invariant weak field of a photon beam
problems.disposition_rationale: A distinctive Chapter 10 parent connecting formal gauge invariance with a concrete null source and physical no-force result; the complete stress-tensor component list and epsilon bookkeeping are essential to the conclusion.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4: for the printed 1+1 dimensional de Sitter and anti-de Sitter metrics, state every coordinate range and compare geodesics, conformal structure, and horizons in an essay.
problems.short_topic: Two-dimensional de Sitter and anti-de Sitter geometry
problems.disposition_rationale: This is another essentially verbatim reuse of 2001 Paper 68 Question 4, including both metrics and the same requested comparison of geodesics, conformal structure, and horizons.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1: prove hypersurface-orthogonality of the normal to beta(x)=0; derive the second-derivative identity for a Killing covector; show the stated Ricci/Killing condition for a static spacetime; and use it with a perfect fluid and rho+p>0 to prove that the fluid four-velocity is parallel to the timelike Killing covector, retaining the supplied Ricci-identity hint.
problems.short_topic: Static Killing fields and perfect-fluid flow
problems.disposition_rationale: A focused Chapter 13 application of hypersurface orthogonality and Killing identities to matter in a static spacetime; the perfect-fluid energy condition and the hinted index convention are necessary hypotheses, not removable context.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: discuss the strong equivalence principle and comma-to-semicolon rule; derive the two printed flat-spacetime vector-potential forms of Maxwell's equation; analyze their inequivalent covariantizations, prove agreement in curved vacuum, and assess whether a terrestrial non-vacuum experiment could resolve the ambiguity using the supplied numerical values of G and Earth's radius.
problems.short_topic: Equivalence principle and curvature ambiguity in Maxwell theory
problems.disposition_rationale: This is a precise and unusually instructive Chapter 3 test of minimal coupling: the two flat identities, their Ricci-curvature difference, the vacuum restriction, and the numerical terrestrial estimate form one indivisible argument.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3: starting from the printed tensor-mode wave equation, supplied retarded-potential solution, far-zone integral, and trace-free stress definition, derive the quadrupole field E^alpha_beta = G Qddot^alpha_beta/r for the printed quadrupole moment and estimate its magnitude for a weak, slowly moving compact source of mass M, size R, and compactness GM/R.
problems.short_topic: Far-zone quadrupole gravitational field
problems.disposition_rationale: A complete Chapter 10 derivation with its central retarded solution and source definitions printed in the question; it also refers to notation from an attached two-sided lecture handout, so a selected transcription must insert any handout convention actually used.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4: compactify Minkowski spacetime using u, v, p, q, T, and R; derive the printed conformal metric; state all coordinate ranges; discuss asymptotic geodesics; and determine its horizon structure.
problems.short_topic: Minkowski conformal boundary and horizons
problems.disposition_rationale: The transformation sequence, range request, geodesic discussion, and horizon question repeat the 2005 version and the canonical 2003 parent with no substantive new mathematical task.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1: derive the relativistic Euler equation from stress-energy conservation; under hydrostatic-equilibrium conditions (a) a timelike Killing symmetry preserving the metric, density, and pressure and (b) flow parallel to the Killing field, normalize the four-velocity and derive the pressure-gradient law; then for black-body radiation p=rho/3 derive rho proportional to (K.K)^-2 and rule out a regular compact free surface.
problems.short_topic: Relativistic hydrostatics of a radiation fluid
problems.disposition_rationale: A coherent hydrodynamics parent for Chapter 5 that carries conservation, Killing equilibrium, an equation of state, and a global consequence through one derivation; both printed equilibrium assumptions are indispensable.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: derive the Newtonian vertical geodesic-deviation equation for two freely falling particles near Earth; add the relative acceleration caused when one particle is charged in a uniform electric field; estimate gravitational and electric changes across a small laboratory; prove gravity becomes negligible as L tends to zero; and use the result for an essay on the strong equivalence principle and relativistic gravity.
problems.short_topic: Laboratory tidal forces and the strong equivalence principle
problems.disposition_rationale: The quantitative comparison of tidal gravity with a nongravitational force gives concrete content to the local limit in Chapter 3; the scaling estimates and final conceptual interpretation must remain together.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3: prove the printed integral identity relating spatial stress to the second derivative of the mass quadrupole; derive the far-zone tensor perturbation and identify r and Q using the supplied retarded-potential hint; then for two equal masses on the stated Newtonian circular orbit derive their positions and angular speed, reproduce the printed trace-free quadrupole matrix, and compute and interpret E^alpha_beta.
problems.short_topic: Quadrupole radiation from an equal-mass circular binary
problems.disposition_rationale: A strong, fully staged Chapter 10 parent that goes beyond the 2007 general derivation by carrying it through a binary source and explicit tensor waveform; the paper permits a lecture handout, so any imported notation or formula must be made self-contained, while the printed retarded hint must be retained verbatim in substance.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4: for the printed 1+1 dimensional de Sitter metric, state the ranges of t and chi, derive and sketch all geodesics through a fixed point, obtain a conformal compactification, and use it to analyze horizons, retaining the supplied transformation T = 2 arctan(e^t) - pi/2.
problems.short_topic: Geodesics and horizons in two-dimensional de Sitter space
problems.disposition_rationale: Unlike the repeated comparative essays, this is a concrete derivation and sketching problem for a maximally symmetric spacetime, with an explicit compactifying hint; no source figure is supplied, so the requested geodesic and conformal diagrams must be constructed in the solution.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1: state the strong equivalence principle, give experimental evidence, and explain its incorporation in general relativity; formulate Newtonian physics on a curved manifold and determine its curvature tensor; and obtain a heuristic perfect-fluid Einstein equation by comparison with the Newtonian case.
problems.short_topic: Geometrized Newtonian gravity and Einstein equations
problems.disposition_rationale: This gives a more mathematical and bounded version of the equivalence-to-field-equations synthesis than the earlier essays by requiring the Newtonian connection and curvature explicitly; all experimental, geometric, and matching stages belong together in Chapter 7.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: derive Killing's equation and the curved-space wave equation for a Killing field from the supplied Ricci identity; use the printed Komar-type surface integral, Stokes and Gauss formulas, and Einstein equations to prove that axisymmetric gravitational waves carry no angular momentum; and prove that the total angular momentum at infinity is independent of the spacelike hypersurface.
problems.short_topic: Komar angular momentum in axisymmetric radiation
problems.disposition_rationale: A rigorous Chapter 7.6 parent combining Killing geometry, the exact surface definition of angular momentum, and two conservation proofs; the orientation conventions and both supplied integral theorems must be retained.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3: derive all null-geodesic equations and constants for the printed Schwarzschild metric, prove equatorial reduction, derive u'^2 = alpha^2 - u^2 + 2u^3, identify alpha, prove the unique circular orbit r=3M, verify the supplied implicit exponential family, and describe its shape as phi tends to minus infinity for each sign of its integration constant.
problems.short_topic: Exact Schwarzschild null geodesics and photon sphere
problems.disposition_rationale: This is a complete exact-geodesic parent for Chapter 8, materially distinct from the 2005 linearized treatment because it includes the photon sphere and an analytic separatrix family; the paper uses the -+++ signature already but its constants still require explicit physical identification.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4: for the printed closed FRW metric and supplied Ricci components, solve the vacuum Einstein equations with cosmological constant, determine the sign of Lambda and time-symmetric scale factor, identify de Sitter spacetime, compactify time with the supplied transformation, draw and label the Penrose diagram with coordinate ranges, and define and determine its particle, event, and Cauchy horizons.
problems.short_topic: Closed de Sitter solution and causal horizons
problems.disposition_rationale: A strong Chapter 16 cosmological-constant parent that derives rather than assumes the de Sitter scale factor and then connects it to conformal and causal structure; the supplied Ricci tensor and requested Penrose diagram are integral source content.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1: for the printed Nordstrom scalar-gravity field equation and conformal physical metric, part (a) derives the Newtonian Poisson equation for pressureless matter and the Newtonian trajectories of slow test bodies; parts (b) and (c) test the theory against Pound-Rebka redshift and solar light bending, with reasons.
problems.short_topic: Newtonian limit and tests of Nordstrom gravity
problems.disposition_rationale: Nordstrom's explicit conformal metric makes this a distinct alternative-gravity test for Chapter 3 rather than a duplicate of the 2006 scalar force law; retaining all of (a)-(c) shows why the Newtonian limit is insufficient to establish a relativistic theory.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: explain gauge freedom for linearized Minkowski perturbations; choose and specify a gauge giving the trace-reversed vacuum wave equation; derive the two-polarization plane-wave form; and compute the proper separation of freely sliding beads on a rigid nonrotating stick for transverse and longitudinal stick orientations.
problems.short_topic: Plane gravitational waves and bead detector
problems.disposition_rationale: A self-contained Chapter 10 parent that ties gauge and polarization analysis directly to detector response; the stick's rigidity, bead initial conditions, propagation direction, and both orientations are essential physical assumptions.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3: derive radial timelike free fall in Schwarzschild spacetime, specialize to release from rest at infinity and compute horizon-to-center proper time, integrate the four-velocity to its proper-time coordinate, derive the printed Painleve-Gullstrand metric, explain removal of the coordinate singularity and contrast it with ingoing Eddington-Finkelstein coordinates, then draw the maximally extended Kruskal diagram and identify the region covered by Painleve-Gullstrand coordinates.
problems.short_topic: Schwarzschild free fall and Painleve-Gullstrand coordinates
problems.disposition_rationale: This is a complete and physically motivated Chapter 8 treatment of horizon-regular coordinates, with the free-fall construction, quantitative proper time, and global coverage linked in one parent; the requested Kruskal diagram must be newly drawn because none is supplied.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4: compactify Minkowski spacetime through u, v, p, q, T, and R; identify the conformal Einstein-static spacetime and state all coordinate ranges; analyze geodesic endpoints; draw and label the Penrose diagram; and determine particle, observer event, and Cauchy horizons with justification.
problems.short_topic: Minkowski conformal boundary and causal horizons
problems.disposition_rationale: The full compactification and asymptotic-geodesic core repeats the 2003 parent, while the added explicit Penrose labels and horizon taxonomy elaborate rather than change that same problem; one canonical expanded adaptation can incorporate those clarifications.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1: part (a)(i) derives Newtonian motion from the printed weak static metric and part (a)(ii) uses the Einstein equation to derive that metric and Poisson law for weak nonrelativistic matter, with permission to quote the linearized equation printed in Question 3; part (b) computes the number of innermost-stable-circular-orbit revolutions a satellite completes before a stated malfunction time T around a Schwarzschild black hole.
problems.short_topic: Weak Newtonian gravity and Schwarzschild ISCO timing
problems.disposition_rationale: The source deliberately combines weak-field motion with a strong-field circular-orbit application, which can serve as a Chapter 8 comparison only if the complete parent is retained; adaptation must insert the exact linearized Einstein equation cross-referenced from Question 3 so that (a)(ii) is self-contained.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2: under an infinitesimal metric variation, parts (a)(i)-(iii) derive the changes in the Levi-Civita connection, Ricci tensor, and Ricci scalar using the supplied coordinate Riemann formula; part (b) varies the printed e^Phi scalar-gravity action with respect to both Phi and the metric and combines the equations to prove R_ab = nabla_a nabla_b Phi, using the supplied determinant-variation identity.
problems.short_topic: Metric variation and dilaton-like gravity action
problems.disposition_rationale: A complete Chapter 12 variation exercise in which the connection and curvature lemmas feed directly into a nonminimal scalar action; all of (a)(i)-(iii), the full action, and the determinant hint are prerequisites for (b).

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3 across printed pages 4-5: parts (a) and (b) derive linearized diffeomorphism gauge symmetry and harmonic gauge; part (c) uses the printed sourced trace-reversed field equation to derive the far-zone quadrupole field and defines I_ij; part (d) states the quadrupole power formula and computes the time-averaged radiation from the specified equal-mass spring oscillator using the supplied point-particle energy density.
problems.short_topic: Gauge, quadrupole field, and spring-source radiation
problems.disposition_rationale: This strong Chapter 10 parent carries the derivation from gauge symmetry through radiation generation and an explicit averaged-power calculation; the page break occurs inside the parent between parts (c) and (d), so neither page may be inventoried or transcribed alone.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4: part (a)(i)-(iii) interprets t=0 in global de Sitter space, constructs its Penrose diagram and I^+ and I^-, and explains cosmological horizons; part (b) defines particle horizons and the FLRW horizon problem; part (c)(i)-(ii) uses the printed Friedmann equation with dust, positive curvature, and Lambda to find the critical static solution and its radius and assess its stability.
problems.short_topic: De Sitter horizons, horizon problem, and Einstein static universe
problems.disposition_rationale: Although broad, all subparts concern causal structure and cosmological-constant models and together form a useful Chapter 16 synthesis; the global metric and Friedmann equation are printed, while the requested Penrose diagram must be generated because no figure accompanies the source.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 1: parts (a) and (b) define covariant derivatives, connection coefficients, torsion freedom, and the Levi-Civita connection and derive its formula; part (c)(i)-(iii), for ds^2 = dr^2 + f(r)^2 dphi^2 with periodic phi, finds the condition for trivial parallel transport around a circle, the two-parameter family making every such circle trivial, proves local Euclidean isometry, and decides global isometry.
problems.short_topic: Levi-Civita connection, holonomy, and global flatness
problems.disposition_rationale: The introductory connection derivation is used immediately in a subtle holonomy-versus-curvature example, making the entire parent a strong Chapter 6 exercise; periodic identification and the distinction between local and global Euclidean geometry cannot be omitted.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 2, parts (a)-(f): define a deviation vector and prove [S,T]=0; state and prove geodesic deviation using the printed Riemann definition; propagate orthogonality of S and the unit timelike tangent T; prove that the scalar curvature in the stated four-dimensional constant-curvature ansatz is constant; derive the conserved K for orthogonal S; and derive the second-order equation for f=S.S and the contrasting exponential behavior for R>0 and R<0.
problems.short_topic: Geodesic deviation in constant-curvature spacetime
problems.disposition_rationale: A comprehensive Chapter 6 parent that joins the abstract deviation equation to an exactly solvable curvature model and qualitative stability; every part (a)-(f) supplies a lemma or invariant needed for the final behavior.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 3: part (a) derives the harmonic-gauge sourced linearized Einstein equation using the supplied coordinate Riemann formula; part (b) determines the restrictions on a complex plane wave, derives residual gauge freedom, and explicitly reduces its polarization matrix to transverse-traceless plus and cross form to justify propagation speed, transversality, and two polarizations; part (c)(i)-(iii) explains why local gravitational stress energy is problematic, constructs a conserved symmetric quadratic tensor from second-order Einstein equations in outline, and explains why it remains unsatisfactory.
problems.short_topic: Linearized waves, TT gauge, and gravitational energy
problems.disposition_rationale: This is a strong Chapter 10 parent extending the usual plane-wave derivation through residual gauge reduction and the conceptual limits of gravitational pseudotensors; all three major parts and the printed polarization matrix belong to one argument.

problems.parent_scope: Complete Question 4: part (a)(i)-(iii) defines Killing fields, derives their geodesic conserved quantity, and lists three independent Killing fields of the printed A(z)^2(-dt^2+dx^2+dy^2)+dz^2 metric; part (b) computes all connection one-forms and curvature two-forms for the supplied orthonormal coframe; part (c) applies Einstein's equation and the null energy condition to prove d^2(log A)/dz^2 <= 0.
problems.short_topic: Warped planar symmetry, tetrad curvature, and null energy
problems.disposition_rationale: The Killing symmetries, coframe calculation, and energy-condition inequality form a single geometric application suitable for Chapter 13; the exact orthonormal coframe and null energy hypothesis are essential, and tetrad sign conversion must follow the edition's conventions.
